h: Holy Eating Makes the Peace of the Heart Endure

p: and you shall dwell in the land securely.
And the land shall give its fruit,
and you shall eat to satiety,
But "you shall dwell in the land securely"
"you shall dwell in the land securely,"
means that they need not fear
the accusation of the yetzer hara;
matters that reason does not require,
so that the words of Torah are engraved in the heart.
such as honoring father and mother,
which even the nations of the world are careful about,
what a certain gentile did, etc."
and I did not serve him
of how Esav served his father, etc."
which is not so with Yisrael,
who fulfill even the rational mitzvos
only to fulfill the command of the Creator,
And this is what is said:
And this is what is said (Tehillim 147:19–20):
His statutes and ordinances to Yisrael;
He has not done so for any nation,
and ordinances they have not known"
that is, they do not bring Daas into them;
"Daas is one who recognizes his Creator,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה נָשֹׂא רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה י)
as stated (Bamidbar Rabbah, Naso, beginning of 10).
that is, they make the words of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג קי, ב)
as stated in the holy Zohar (III 110b):
as it were, you shall make them"
"And you shall dwell in the land securely":
that the yetzer hara be uprooted from the heart.
one is still not entirely secure,
for at the Giving of the Torah
the yetzer hara was uprooted from the heart
with the utterance "You shall not have,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה פָּרָשַׁת יִשָּׁקֵנִי)
as stated (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:2, "Let him kiss me"),
the yetzer hara returned to its place.
And about this it is said:
"And the land shall give its fruit,
and you shall eat to satiety."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (מִשְׁלֵי יג, כה)
And this is according to what is said (Mishlei 13:25):
"The tzaddik eats to satisfy his soul";
יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית כח, כ)
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him (Bereishis 28:20):
"and He will give me bread to eat
that Hashem Yisbarach is the One who gives,
the eating will be in holiness.
And this is what is said:
"And the land shall give its fruit"
the land of the Holy One, blessed be He,
"the tzaddik eats to satisfy his soul";
that is, that there will be
and I will grant peace in the land,
and you shall lie down with none to make you afraid"
that they will no longer fear
of the war of the yetzer hara;
where the eating is in holiness
from the accusation of the yetzer hara,
and it is expounded (in the Mechilta, Yisro)
a person is guarded from sin;
and in Pri Etz Chaim the wording is
that one is saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara,

An Uprooted Inclination Can Still Return
